model_player_facing_text: Rain spatters the soot-dark stones above Cinderwatch's eastern gate, where frayed banners flutter weakly in the chilly wind. The muddy approach outside the gate is clogged with refugees, wagons heavy with goods, and the constant shuffle of travelers, all pressing forward under the watchful eyes of guards holding the narrow choke point firm. Nearby, a notice board commands attention, its posted papers listing new taxes, curfew rules, and a stark warning about a missing patrol. A well-appointed townhouse presides over the square in quiet contrast to the clamoring crowd. Off to one side, a figure in threadbare clothes remains almost motionless, their gaze flicking uneasily to faces and packs more than the gate itself. Amidst the murmurs, a tavern runner nearby pitches hot stew and fresh rumors, his voice cutting through the damp air, promising news for a coin. The weight of official watchfulness and uncertain rumors hang in the moisture-heavy air as you stand at the fringe of this gathering.

"Aye," the tavern runner nods, glancing around before lowering his voice. "Word is, that patrol vanished near some muddy footprints northwest of the crates outside the gate. I can't say what happened for sure, but they just never came back. Folks say it's worth watching that spot if you're planning to seek answers."

"From what I gathered," the guard captain says quietly, "several gate guards spotted those footprints just this morning near the crates northwest of the entrance. A couple of them were sent out to investigate, but they came back without word—no sign of the patrol or what became of them. So far, the talk you're hearing is mostly rumors swirling among travelers and refugees, patchy and unsettled." They glance toward the muddy approach, their expression tight. "If you want answers, the northwest track past the crates is where to start looking."

The guard captain narrows their eyes, considering your questions carefully. "No one from the gate watch has actually gone to inspect those footprints yet," they say quietly. "Locals and travelers passing through noticed them earlier this morning near the northwest crates. The timing matches when the patrol last checked in before disappearing. If you’re thinking of investigating, that’s the direction to head."

"The watch hasn't sent anyone to investigate the footprints yet," the guard captain says with a tight expression. "That patrol was assigned to the usual perimeter check northwest of the crates, but they vanished before their next scheduled report. As for why no one has gone to look, I can only say that orders haven't come down from higher up to dispatch a search party so far." They glance toward the crowded gate and lower their voice. "If you're serious about following up, you might start by checking the old milestone to the northwest — travelers say the patrol was last seen heading that way."

The guard captain glances briefly toward the cluster of gate guards and serjeants around the crowded gate. "We're waiting on orders from the city watch commander," they say quietly, voice low as if wary of nearby ears. "No official word yet on whether to investigate the missing patrol or to let the matter rest for now."

The captain's narrowed eyes flick toward the notice board listing the missing patrol warning. "If you're heading out to that milestone," they add carefully, "be ready for whatever. No one knows for sure what happened, and the brass seems hesitant to stir the hornet's nest."

The guard captain lowers their voice further, glancing cautiously toward the gate cluster before meeting your eyes. "It's the brass's term for the trouble brewing beyond that old milestone northwest of here. They're afraid of what might surface if anyone pokes around—old secrets, unsettled scores, things better left buried, as the saying goes. Orders came down hard not to stir the hornet's nest until higher command weighs in. If someone goes, they want it carefully, not recklessly. That’s why the watch is waiting—for clarity and caution."

You hold the guard captain's steady gaze, voice lowered with the rain-slicked tension around you. The captain exhales quietly, eyes flicking briefly toward the cluster of guards and the crowded gate. "Old secrets and unsettled scores," they murmur, "belong mostly to city watch brass and those who whisper in shadow—noble intrigues tangled with unspoken debts. Around the gate, no one openly talks; the brass has sealed lips tight. If anyone here knows more, they've learned well the price of loose tongues." Your best lead would be to press local informants or seek someone with ties to the city watch command—perhaps the tavern runner or a more discreet contact beyond the gate crowd."

The tavern runner gives a cautious glance below the rain, voice low and laced with a mix of respect and wariness. "Past that old milestone, debts weave through the families like smoke—noble quarrels, too, but those are often whispered, cloaked behind veils and favors. Loose tongues aren’t taken lightly; speaking out can cost you far more than coin—sometimes your reputation, sometimes worse. Best not to ask too many questions without a careful ear and a good friend—or a thick purse to pay for silence."

"Names and debts? That's a tough one to pin down," the tavern runner replies, voice low and cautious beneath the steady rain. "Families, sure — old bloodlines like the Durains or the Velmarks have tangled grudges, and their debts? They're not the kind you'd settle at the market. But no honest soul talks openly about who might silence a patrol."

He shifts slightly, eyes flicking toward the gate guards. "If you want a name, you'd do better to start by shadowing the rumors past the old milestone northwest of the crates. That's where trouble’s been simmering, and that's what some say keeps patrols from sending reports back."

"But be careful—ask too much too loud, and you'd find yourself needing that thick purse to pay for silence."

The tavern runner shakes their head, eyes flickering with a mix of caution and old suspicion. "I can’t pin it to one family or debt," they say, voice low. "The troubles beyond that milestone are tangled up with many old scores and whispered deals—too many shadows for any one name to hold." They glance around briefly. "If you want names, you’ll need someone with deeper roots and thicker pockets than mine."

"You'll want to keep your ears open for the families tied longest to this place, though few speak freely," the ragged stranger says quietly, nodding toward the cluster near the gate guard posts. "Noble houses like Verevin and shadowed groups like the Ash Cowl — both play dangerous games here. But talk? They won’t warm up to just any stranger, especially one with a thin purse." They glance sideways, voice dropping. "Silence often costs less than a coin, though it’s a rare favor to earn."

The ragged stranger glances toward the quieter fringe of the square where you indicate, then shakes their head. "Not somewhere I can name," they say quietly, voice edged with hesitation. "Whoever it is, they watch too closely. Better to keep their names out of this muddy rain."

The square remains soaked and restless below frayed banners, the notice board nearby casting little comfort with its lists of taxes, curfews, and a warning about the missing patrol.
